title: Module deprecation timeline and compatibility checklist (notes)
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a working notes doc for module deprecation timelines, registry publishing checklist, and compatibility guidance for private/on‑prem deployments. Goal: reduce customer disruption when module changes are required (API/inputs/outputs), and capture a pragmatic rolling upgrade + rollback process for modules we publish to the internal registry (and optionally to public registries).

Scope (what this covers):
- Terraform modules used in Private and VPC/on‑prem packages (networking, kube bootstrap, ingress, kms, monitoring agents).
- Versioning policy, deprecation cadence, canary publish & smoke tests, rollback plan, consumer migration helpers, and CI gating.
- Not covering provider version pinning (separate doc).

Key principles (short):
- Backwards-compatibility-first: prefer additive changes.
- When breaking changes are unavoidable, provide a clear migration path and at least 2 weeks of parallel support for older module versions for Dedicated/Private customers.
- All breaking changes must have a CHERRY-PICKABLE migration example in the module repo and a runnable test plan.
- Publishing to internal registry is gated by automated contract tests + SRE sign‑off.

Semantic versioning & exceptions:
- We use SemVer-ish version numbers for modules: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.
  - PATCH: bug fixes, non-functional tweaks.
  - MINOR: new optional inputs/outputs, new resources guarded by vars, non-breaking improvements.
  - MAJOR: incompatible changes (rename/remove input/output, change resource shape).
- Exception: if a performance/latency/security fix must be applied immediately, we may push a MAJOR that is fast‑tracked but must still follow the Canary + Notice process.

Deprecation timeline (recommended):
1. Draft PR with breaking change + migration examples (0 days)
2. Publish to internal registry with pre-release tag (e.g., 2.0.0-beta.1) and mark in CHANGELOG (day 0)
3. Canary stage: two internal customers or internal staging clusters enabled to use beta for 7–14 days; run contract tests daily (day 1–14)
4. Announce deprecation: post notice to #private-deployments Slack + customer success for any affected customers (day 3)
5. Lock change with migration guide and sample commits (day 7)
6. After successful canary + no regressions, publish GA (2.0.0) and keep 1.x branch alive for at least 14 days with backports for critical fixes (day 14)
7. After 30 days final reminder before sunset of old major; archive example repos that relied on old behavior, and open follow‑up tickets for customers who need more time.

Registry publishing checklist (internal registry):
- Prepublish (local):
  - Run terraform fmt and tflint across module.
  - Update README + CHANGELOG with migration steps and examples (copy/paste runnable HCL).
  - Add compatibility matrix in README: tested terraform core versions and known provider versions.
  - Add explicit example root module showing how to consume both old and new module (use different workspaces).
- CI gating (must pass):
  - unit tests (terratest/suite) run in PR for both old and new version integration points.
  - contract test (see below) — run for recorded inputs/outputs.
  - publish job dry run: build artifact + verify tag naming.
  - automatic changelog entry via conventional commits.
- Canary publish:
  - Push pre-release to internal registry (x.y.z-beta.N).
  - Create a canary plan doc (short) and assign owners.
  - Trigger smoke pipeline: apply example root against internal staging account(s).
  - Run health checks: resource count sanity, IP assignments, IAM bindings, networking connectivity tests.
- GA publish:
  - Publish semver release to registry with release notes.
  - Update internal module index page and tag repos.
  - Notify stakeholders: eng, SRE, Solutions Eng, Customer Success.
  - Add to platform upgrade plan if module is used by Redwood-managed VPC images.

Breaking-change checklist (to include in PR template):
- [ ] Title begins with BREAKING: brief summary.
- [ ] Migration guide attached to PR (README/migrating.md).
- [ ] Example root change(s) minimal and copy‑paste runnable.
- [ ] Contract tests added/updated (see contract tests section).
- [ ] Compatibility metadata updated (supported terraform versions/providers).
- [ ] Deprecation plan: timeline (dates) and responsible owners named.
- [ ] Internal announcement draft included (Slack + CS email).
- [ ] Rollback plan documented (how to pin to previous module and patch).
- [ ] CI: canary pipelines configured to run against beta tags.

Contract tests (recommended pattern):
- Purpose: detect behavioral changes to module public surface (inputs → diffs/outputs).
- Approach: maintain a small set of golden example roots per module that run in ephemeral test accounts and assert expected resources and outputs.
- Tests should be idempotent and fast (<10 minutes ideally). If heavy resources are needed, run nightly and add a lightweight smoke test for PRs.
- Example outputs to assert: specific output names, types (map/list/string), and essential resource attributes (security_group IDs count, subnet CIDR masks, kms key alias).

Consumer migration helpers (to include in repo):
- A tiny helper script migrate-rename-inputs.sh that shows sed/patch pattern to rename old var -> new var in root modules (copy/paste).
- A Terraform null_resource example that keeps old input names mapped to new ones for one intermediate release (compat shim).
- A Terragrunt snippet showing how to pin module version in a root config and run a canary workspace.

Examples (copy/paste):
- How to pin module in root module (HCL snippet):
  module "network" {
    source = "registry.internal.redwood.dev/infra/network/aws"
    version = "~> 1.3" # pin minor during migration window
    vpc_cidr = var.vpc_cidr
  }

- Simple compat shim pattern (HCL snippet):
  // in module root: variables.tf defines new var 'subnet_prefixes' but we accept old 'subnet_list' for one release
  locals {
    subnet_prefixes_resolved = length(var.subnet_prefixes) > 0 ? var.subnet_prefixes : var.subnet_list
  }

Communication & stakeholder process:
- At PR open for breaking change: Slack announcement to #private-deployments and ping Solutions Eng for customer impact.
- 1st week: Solutions Eng runs targeted migration with 1–2 customers (opt-in).
- 2nd week: broader internal canary, CS notifies customers using module via customer inventory (tagging in repo).
- Post-GA: send customer email with migration steps + offer support sessions.

Rollback plan (if GA causes regression):
- Step 1: Revert consuming root module to pin to previous module (e.g., version = "~>1.5.3") and apply.
- Step 2: Open incident ticket, capture tfplan/taints, and coordinate hotfix branch for module.
- Step 3: If necessary, publish a 2.x.1 patch that reintroduces previous behavior behind a feature flag var and communicate to customers.

CI job names (suggested):
- module-ci/unit-tests
- module-ci/contract-smoke-pr
- module-ci/canary-deploy-staging
- module-ci/publish-dryrun
- module-ci/publish-ga

Sample commit message guidelines (conventional commits):
- feat(module): add optional field `enable_ipv6` (non-breaking)
- fix(module): correct IAM role policy expansion (patch)
- BREAKING(module): rename input `cluster_name` -> `infra_cluster_name`
- chore(release): publish v2.0.0

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want an API that maps customer inventory to module usage automatically? (helps CS identify impacted customers)
- Agree on minimum support window for old majors (14 days vs 30 days).
- Decide whether we push pre-release tags to external public registries for community modules or keep them internal until GA.
- Add an automated changelog generator to the publish pipeline (we currently rely on PR text).

Quick reference: minimal migration checklist for Solutions Eng (two‑pager):
1) Read migration guide + run example root in a disposable workspace.
2) Validate outputs and run smoke tests (connectivity, ACLs).
3) If failure, collect tfplan & resource diff and open JIRA PD-xxx with logs.
4) Help customer pin to previous module and schedule assisted migration session.

Appendix: recommended CHANGELOG template (top of release note):
- Release: vX.Y.Z (YYYY-MM-DD)
- Type: GA | beta | patch
- Summary: short 1–2 sentence description
- Breaking changes: bullet list + migration examples
- Deprecations: inputs/outputs flagged and when they will be removed
- Tests ran: list of smoke/contract tests and pass status
- Contacts: owner email + SRE oncall alias

-- end notes --

Notes to self (todo rough):
- Wire up a Confluence page with a module inventory export.
- Draft an email template for CS to send when module GA happens.
- Add a terraform-provider-compatibility section to every module README.
